items.title: Regular Agenda
Strategic Focus – Healthy, Safe and Inclusive Communities
CSD-HOU-23-019, Building Better Futures, Update and Roadmap to 2,500 Affordable Homes
notes:
Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community Health Services, introduced the report CSD-HOU-23-019, Building Better Futures, Update and Roadmap to 2,500 Affordable Homes and he highlighted that during the 2023 budget process the Region had set the goal to build 2,500 new affordable housing units over five years. Ryan Pettipiere, Director, Housing Services provided a brief update on the progress of this goal and the successes thus far. He estimated that Staff are in progress to build units than the initial goal.

Craig Dyer, Commissioner of Corporate Services discussed the financial implications of funding the Waterloo Region housing master plan project, specifically, the challenges with respect to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation as there is currently no further funding available for ongoing projects. He noted that there will have to be amendments to the sources of funding for these projects, since the CMHC will not be providing the anticipated funding that was budgeted for. He explained that external funding is difficult to predict and that advocating to both the federal and provincial governments is vital to maintain ongoing and future projects.

In response to the Committee, C. Dyer explained that the lack of funding from the CMHC will have the most predominate impact on the 2025 budget.

The Committee expressed the importance of external partners in continuing the progress in housing initiatives, specifically the necessity of supportive housing.

Received for information.

items.title: Strategic Focus – Responsive and Engaging Public Service
CAO-EDI-23-002, Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group and Equity-Based Collaboration
notes:
Fauzia Baig, Director, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion, Paula Whitlow, Director, Truth & Reconciliation, provided a presentation on the CAO-EDI-23-002, Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group and Equity-Based Collaboration report. F. Baig highlighted background on  ARAWG and the Group's mandate. P. Whitlow summarized Regional Council's previous and ongoing related projects including the Regional approval of $10 million for the equity investing funding. F. Baig noted that Staff are working on creating REDI Action Partnership which will assist in community and Staff coordination to facilitate Regional positive change. P. Whitlow further noted that an objective is to update the current smudging policy to permit its use in more wide ranging events.

C. James provided a motion that the Committee considered following waiving notice. The Committee noted that members should avoid presenting motions without notice whenever possible.

Received for information.

motions.item_title: CAO-EDI-23-002, Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group and Equity-Based Collaboration
motions.text: WHEREAS Regional Council is committed to addressing anti-racism and advancing Truth and Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion; and WHEREAS the Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group (ARAWG) was created in 2020 to advise Regional Council on how to address systemic racism present in regional policies, procedures, and practices; and WHEREAS the Region as a result of the Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group has hired a Director of Equity, Diversity & Inclusion and a Director of Truth & Reconciliation; and WHEREAS continued work is required to engage residents, community partners and municipalities in anti-racism work; and WHEREAS this work needs to be decentralized and embedded within the way the Region operates; THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED That the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) of the Region of Waterloo consider ways to further embed Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in Regional operations and community engagement, including options for: The continuation and expansion of a fixed team of community connectors specific to anti-racism, equity and reconciliation initiatives in the region of waterloo. To collaboratively work with staff and a newly formed Reconciliation Equity Diversity Inclusion (REDI) Action Partnership to further create a process for transparency and accountability in decision making. The roles of the Director, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion and Director, Truth & Reconciliation be included as part of the Region’s Corporate Leadership Team. That a copy of this resolution and the committee report be circulated to area municipalities so it can inform their work on Truth and Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS Regional Council is committed to addressing anti-racism and advancing Truth and Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion; and

WHEREAS the Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group (ARAWG) was created in 2020 to advise Regional Council on how to address systemic racism present in regional policies, procedures, and practices; and

WHEREAS the Region as a result of the Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group has hired a Director of Equity, Diversity & Inclusion and a Director of Truth & Reconciliation; and

WHEREAS continued work is required to engage residents, community partners and municipalities in anti-racism work; and

WHEREAS this work needs to be decentralized and embedded within the way the Region operates;

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED

  1. That the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) of the Region of Waterloo consider ways to further embed Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in Regional operations and community engagement, including options for:
    1. The continuation and expansion of a fixed team of community connectors specific to anti-racism, equity and reconciliation initiatives in the region of waterloo. To collaboratively work with staff and a newly formed Reconciliation Equity Diversity Inclusion (REDI) Action Partnership to further create a process for transparency and accountability in decision making.
    2. The roles of the Director, Equity, Diversity & Inclusion and Director, Truth & Reconciliation be included as part of the Region’s Corporate Leadership Team.
  2. That a copy of this resolution and the committee report be circulated to area municipalities so it can inform their work on Truth and Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion.
